Severe hair loss in Satoyoshi syndrome can progress to complete loss of scalp and body hair (alopecia universalis), presumed to reflect autoimmune follicular injury.
Secondary skeletal abnormalities and mandibular condylar degeneration co-occur with severe painful muscle spasms and are considered downstream musculoskeletal sequelae.

evidence.reference_title: Impending central retinal vein occlusion and granulomatous uveitis in a patient with Satoyoshi syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Unilateral granulomatous pan-uveitis and impending CRVO were observed in this patient. Several cases of Satoyoshi syndrome complicated by various autoimmune or immunological disorders have been reported. However, to the best of our knowledge, no reports of Satoyoshi syndrome presenting with uveitis or CRVO have been published. Physicians should consider uveitis as a complication of Satoyoshi syndrome.
